#1746. Mac Allister not so sad now after Liverpool comeback winner

Do your talking on the pitch, as the old adage goes, and Alexis Mac Allister emphatically did just that as Liverpool came from behind to thrillingly win their first Champions League tie under new head coach Andoni Iraola in what was his debut at this level.

On the eve of this encounter, against a strong Atlético Madrid, one of the clubs who have recently tried to sign him, Mac Allister had spoken of his sadness. Sadness that, unlike fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai – Liverpool’s other scorer here – and Ryan Gravenberch, he had not been offered and signed a new contract.

So, earn it. And many more goals – and overall performances like this – there is no doubt the Argentinian will have a deal placed in front of him. He scored with an arresting second-half shot, which proved to be the winner, and the smile across his face said it all. Not so sad now as he was later substituted to a standing ovation with Gravenberch taking his place.

The goal came early in the second half, with Iraola attributing that to adjusting his tactics after being flummoxed by Atlético’s back five and packed midfield in a first half when Liverpool were second best.

Mac Allister was heavily involved through the build-up, eventually picking out Rio Ngumoha on the left whose shot was blocked and pinballed around. It dropped to Mac Allister, 20 yards out, and he hit the kind of unerring drive that gives the goalkeeper no chance. And so it proved. Boom. And Anfield was bouncing.

Mac Allister FIRES Liverpool into the lead at Anfield! 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/KGOvuAEU4W

There are certainly signs under Iraola, and following a difficult last campaign, that Mac Allister is beginning to rediscover the form he showed during his first two seasons at Liverpool. Time and again the 27-year-old made vital interventions, showed aggression and walked the tightrope of a harsh early yellow card. He dovetailed with Szoboszlai and that might be a concern for Gravenberch – watched by the Netherlands’ new head coach Xavi Hernández – if Iraola persists with this approach.

Although Mac Allister has two years left on his current deal, the last thing Liverpool need is yet another attention-sapping contract saga, even if he is not the same scale of player as Mohamed Salah or Trent Alexander-Arnold.

For Iraola, after three Premier League games, comprising two draws and a victory over newly-promoted Ipswich Town, this will hopefully be lift off. A big European night at Anfield and coming from behind to beat one of the continent’s heavyweights.

“I loved it,” Iraola said, before castigating himself for misreading the way Atlético would line up. And what of Mac Allister’s riposte? There was a smile from Iraola before the Spaniard’s usual diplomacy kicked in as he talked about a “lovely, lovely goal” and how good it was for his midfielders to contribute.

Liverpool had to fight for it and what will have satisfied Iraola is that the defence, which has come under such scrutiny, held out. Even so, there are still serious concerns over the suitability of Milos Kerkez at left-back – who was badly at fault for Atlético’s goal – although the robust Ronald Araújo showed he can be a strong and versatile option on the other flank. The Uruguayan, signed on loan from Barcelona, is such a presence in both penalty areas and has the capacity to gain cult status.

As does £123m signing from Paris St-Germain Bradley Barcola, who should have scored – once, certainly, possibly twice – and possesses astonishing pace that will undoubtedly lead to goals. There are also encouraging signs that his presence could enliven Florian Wirtz. Barcola eventually also went off, but thankfully it was only to cramp.

There was a collective intake of breath across the Kop when Marcos Llorente was played through and bore down on them to give Atlético the lead. There was a desperate hope that he had strayed offside. There was then a realisation that Kerkez had, however, played him on with an appalling lack of awareness. Llorente beat Alisson.

It owed much to a wonderful shimmy, deceiving Szoboszlai in centre field, by Julián Alvarez before he smartly threaded the ball through, and Mac Allister’s international team-mate almost doubled Atlético’s advantage soon after. Only to be denied by Alisson.

Llorente breaks the deadlock! 🔥That's now FIVE Champions League goals for the Atletico man against Liverpool at Anfield 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/Rxp4zurfpc

We knew, we feared it would be Llorente who scored. Remarkably, he has now half of his 10 goals in this competition against Liverpool. Indeed, he named his dog Anfield after his extra-time brace knocked Liverpool, then the holders, out in the last 16 in 2020. And Liverpool had made a dog’s dinner of defending this time.

This is a different Atlético. A far less defensive, far more expansive Atlético. In years gone by, once they were 1-0 it was game over under Diego Simeone. But these days they try and play more and that gives their opponents a chance. And so it proved.

Atlético goalkeeper Jan Oblak did well to deny Barcola, with his trailing foot, before Wirtz won the ball back and found Szoboszlai who eventually ended the movement. It owed much, however, to a clever backheel to pick out the midfielder who finished low into the corner. Who executed that backheel? That would be Araújo.

Barcola should have scored, sent clear by Wirtz in a brilliant, sweeping counter-attack, before Mac Allister did.

The question now was whether Liverpool would show the resilience to see through the result. As Iraola made changes, they answered that with a resounding yes, which will have pleased him as much as the result, as much as the comeback, as much as Mac Allister’s stunning response.

“I was enjoying it [the Anfield crowd]. They [Atletico Madrid] are a very good team. Technically, in the middle, lovely players. It is not easy to press those players as they have quality. Diego Simeone most wonder how Atleti are losing a game they were controlling but Liverpool’s speed on the break is proving very good at causing chaos.

Barcola should have his first Liverpool goal and the hosts should be ahead but the Frenchman misses the target. Barcola drives forward, into the Atletico box, and you think he is going to slot it into the bottom corner but his effort goes just wide. Barcola could and perhaps should have a brace tonight.

Barcola wins the first corner of this second half off Hancko right in front of The Kop. Liverpol take it short before Mac Allister clips the ball in. Araujo meets it and his header is powerful but it is off target.

But the “talismanic” piece of football memorabilia ended up being sold by auctioneer Budds for £149,500 to a UK private buyer.

The Argentine is into the final two years of his contract, which runs out in 2028. He arrived at Liverpool in the same summer as fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai, who have both signed new contracts. Mac Allister was linked with a move away from Liverpool during the summer transfer window and was candid about his contractual situation in the press conference yesterday:

“I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract which, of course, makes me very, very sad. Everyone can see that I give my 100% for this football club every single day in training and games. Of course, I can have very good games [and] bad games, like everyone, but I always give my best.

“I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch] renewing their contracts and that makes me very happy because they deserve it. At the same time it makes me a little bit sad that I did not get mine. Of course, there is still time. The fans do not need to worry because I will give my 100% until the last day I am here. There were options to leave this summer. I think right now I am in the right club and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club.”

Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez, who led the club to Champions League glory on that famous night in Istanbul in 2005, is in attendance tonight. Andoni Iraola has just shared a hug with his compatriot and perhaps Benitez will have a few words of advice for Iraola ahead of his Champions League debut as a manager.

When Liverpool won their sixth European Cup in 2019, they lifted it in the Wanda Metropolitano against Tottenham. This season’s Champions League final is in that very stadium and Liverpool’s Champions League campaign starts tonight against the club that plays their home games in that stadium, Atletico Madrid.

“This is going to be a challenge, I hope, all the season because it would mean we continue in all the competitions. In this case, it is not the worst scenario because we played last Friday so we have had I think a good recovery. Probably it is going to be more difficult for next weekend, especially for the next game against Tottenham in the Carabao Cup because we will have just two days, game, two days, game. Liverpool begin their Champions League campaign at home as they host Atletico Madrid at Anfield. These sides met at Anfield on matchday one last season, with Liverpool winning a dramatic game 3-2. Liverpool led 2-0 inside the opening 10 minutes before Atletico came back to level the game at 2-2. Virgil van Dijk then scored in added time to give Liverpool all three points before Atletico boss Diego Simeone was sent off for clashing with the Anfield crowd, resulting in a one-match ban.

Andoni Iraola earned his first win as Liverpool boss on Friday night as they won 2-0 away at Ipswich thanks to a quickfire early double from Alexander Isak. This will be Iraola’s first Champions League match as a manager.

“I think obviously it is a special night for me,” Iraola said. “Everyone talks [about] the Champions League nights at Anfield and also the first game is against a strong opposition, it is Atletico Madrid. [Diego] Simeone is doing an incredible job as a manager. To be all the years that he has been achieving every season the goals of the club I think is remarkable and definitely it is a big challenge for us. I think I played against him as a player, he was still a player, and I played against his teams when he was a coach and I also coached against him. So, we had a lot of precedent before. Definitely he has much more experience than me in this kind of games but I hope tomorrow we can give him a good game.

“It is one of the dreams, probably, when you start. It was difficult for me when I started my coaching career seven, eight years ago, to position myself in the position that I am right now, and I hope I can enjoy it. It is a big responsibility, massive challenge, but I feel privileged to be there in that dugout tomorrow [tonight] and now my thinking is about putting the team together in a position where we can play a good game, win the game and start strong in this Champions League.”

Atletico Madrid currently sit sixth in La Liga and suffered their first defeat on Saturday as they lost 3-0 at Athletic Bilbao. They did reach the semi-finals of the Champions League last season, where they fell to Arsenal 2-1 on aggregate.

“We are coming into a marvellous stadium and there will be a great atmosphere,” Simeone said. “We will have to look good from the start of the game because it will be full on. He [Andoni Iraola] works very well with the team, focusing on the tactical awareness of each player. It takes time to find the right path, but he is growing and improving and he has some very good players.”

#1745. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

#1744. Tuttosport: Milan considering return attempt with Athekame with talks expected in January

AC Milan are beginning to explore the possibility of an early return for Zachary Athekame, after his start to life in France.

When they signed Athekame in the summer of 2025, Milan were aware that he was a player for the future. Nevertheless, he was still given occasional minutes last season and he could’ve been given more.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

He also could’ve stayed this season; in hindsight, things are viewed differently. Yet, there would be an argument that he’d have provided some quality depth in a position of makeshift options.

According to Tuttosport this morning, via MilanPress, the Rossoneri would be keen to bring Athekame back from his loan spell in France early for several reasons. Firstly, the Swiss has reached a new level in France this season, so his return would be a permanent one.

Then, the injury issues mean that the squad is weak at full-back. So, with Ruben Amorim looking to a four-back system more frequently, he could help a lot.

It won’t be as easy as just recalling him, though. Lyon still need to be convinced and there was no agreement for his return before the summer. With this, the French club have already hinted that a fee would be required for an early return.

Talks are expected to take place in January and with Paulo Fonseca leaving the club, Athekame’s perspective on things could change. We shall have to see.

#1743. Lisandro Martinez was stupid, selfish and let the club down: Man United fans may have loved 'The Butcher' but losing his head is the latest act on the road to a bitter Old Trafford exit, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 22:00 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 22:00 EDT, 31 October 2026

To borrow a phrase from Lisandro Martinez, we expect more from him.

We expect more from a vastly experienced defender and World Cup winner. We expect more from a 28-year-old whose team-mates during a stellar career include Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo.

We expect more from Martinez than to fling an arm into the face of an opponent in the penalty box a matter of seconds after being booked for another offence with such a crucial game hanging in the balance.

How did he think he was going to get away with it? How did he think it was going to help Manchester United’s chances of staying out of the relegation zone or Michael Carrick’s prospects of keeping his job?

Just when Carrick needed cool heads among his senior players, Martinez went and lost his.

No sooner had his arm connected with Wesley Fofana than VAR official James Bell sent referee Peter Bankes to the monitor. A second yellow card followed and a penalty for Cole Palmer to convert Chelsea's second goal. Game over.

When Michael Carrick needed cool heads, Lisandro Martinez (right) went and lost his

He finds himself at the scene of the crime too often and his time at the club appears to be coming to an end

There was no way back for United from there, not in their current fragile state.

Carrick couldn’t say what he really thought of Martinez’s moment of madness, but legendary United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel did it for him.

'I put this solely on Lisandro Martinez's shoulders,' fumed Schmeichel. 'This is an absolute disgrace how he played this game. The penalty, I have no words for how crazy that was. Then he walks off the pitch shaking his head like he's done nothing wrong. So bad.'

This is the same Martinez who landed himself with a club fine earlier this month for saying he expected more of United’s director of football Jason Wilcox in the transfer market last summer.

The same Martinez who scored a hapless own-goal down the road from Chelsea at Fulham in September. The same Martinez who turned his back on the ball against Tottenham a week earlier, and allowed Dominic Solanke to score a late equaliser at Old Trafford.

With his contract running out in June, and no sign of United intending to trigger a 12-month extension clause, it looks as though his time at United is coming to an end and not in the way he would have wanted.

‘Whatever the next Man United phase is, I think Martinez's time at the club has run its course,’ Joe Cole told TNT Sports. ‘In a Man United shirt, he's just at the scene of the crime too often.’

No doubt Martinez’s resentment over his contract situation played a part in his comment about Wilcox. While supporters have applauded him for calling out the club’s recruitment – and there is no doubt he has a point – his time would be better spent focussing on keeping the ball out of United’s net and keeping himself on the pitch rather than pointing the finger at others.

He has been one of United’s better signings of recent years, albeit one hampered by a succession of unfortunate injuries. The combative edge and winning mentality he brought from his time with Argentina and Ajax have been an asset to Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and, to a lesser extent, Carrick.

Michael Carrick (left) could not say what he really thought but was let down by one of his more senior players

The fans love The Butcher and you can see why at a time when so many players who have passed through the doors during his five years at Old Trafford have failed to show enough heart for the fight

But this was a stupid, selfish act borne out of frustration which cost United any chance of winning this game and will keep Martinez out of United’s last fixture before the international break at home to Aston Villa next weekend.

By the time they return to action, there is no guarantee Carrick will still be in a job.

If you want to compare Michael Carrick’s successful spell in charge at United last season with the seemingly inexplicable drop-off this term, this was exactly the kind of marginal game that he was winning back then.

Think of Carrick’s first two matches in charge against Manchester City and Arsenal, and the 3-2 wins over Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Fulham. Perhaps most relevant of all, the 1-0 win here over Chelsea in April when Matheus Cunha scored the only goal just before half-time.

If United had taken only half their chances in the first half at Stamford Bridge this time, they could have put the game to bed. Amad Diallo had enough of them to win it on his own.

It would be easy to say that Carrick’s luck has run out but it isn’t that easy in elite sport. The confidence that flowed through the team in those months between January and May has drained from his players. Chances are being missed, silly goals conceded. Experienced campaigners like Martinez are suffering from a rush of blood to the head, and every mistake is being punished. That’s what happens when the tide turns and you haven’t got the resilience to ride it out.

Every game looks hard for United at the moment. Their only victories this season have been at home to Sabah and Ipswich, and even the latter came with a slice of luck.

Who knows where their next win is coming from? As he left West London looking rather dazed, Carrick didn’t seem like a man who has the answer to that question.

It feels like Bruno Fernandes's great Manchester United career may be coming to an end

Once we knew Carrick would be in the dugout at Stamford Bridge, all the talk in the build-up to this game was about the return of captain Bruno Fernandes after he was dropped for last weekend’s defeat to Bournemouth.

Fernandes didn’t just come back into the line-up, he was back at No10 after vacating that role for Youri Tielemans in recent weeks. Tielemans was deservedly left on the bench here while Fernandes interchanged with Cunha in a fluid United attack that performed well in a promising first half.

But the Fernandes of old would have made his mark on this game. Got a goal or an assist to lead his team to victory and ram the taunts of rival fans down their throats.

But he did nothing of the sort. Too many passes went astray, too often the arms were thrown up in the air in frustration. When he had a great chance to put United ahead in the first half from Bryan Mbeumo’s brilliant pass, Fernandes blazed it over the bar.

One man can’t carry an entire team, but the Portugal star has come close to it at times during his seven-year career at Old Trafford. Here, though, was more evidence that his powers may be fading and this United team may be beyond help.

United were open to selling Fernandes to Al-Hilal last year and won’t break the bank to keep him when his current deal runs out in June. They might renew at the right price or at least trigger the 12-month option to make sure he doesn’t leave on a free transfer.

But it feels like a great United career may be coming to an end.

#1741. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

The Vasil Levski National Stadium will host Thursday’s Europa League clash between Bulgarian champions Levski Sofia and Polish outfit Jagiellonia Bialystok.

Both sides head into the encounter in good recent form, but a victory would provide a significant boost to their hopes of reaching the knockout stage.

Julio Velazquez is approaching his second anniversary at Levski Sofia, and the Spanish coach continues to impress since taking charge of the Bulgarian giants.

Levski are currently on a six-match unbeaten run across all competitions, winning four of those matches and scoring nine goals along the way.

Their last defeat came against Red Bull Salzburg in their Europa League opener, with the Bulgarian champions suffering a 1-0 loss in a game where they failed to register a single shot on target.

Remarkably, that was also their last outing on home turf, with Velazquez and his men embarking on a run of six consecutive away matches.

Even then, it was not their usual home ground, as Levski have been forced to relocate from the Georgi Asparuhov Stadium to the Vasil Levski National Stadium for their European fixtures.

Nevertheless, the Bulgarian champions will now be hoping to take another step towards reaching the knockout stage of a European competition for the first time since their memorable 2005-06 UEFA Cup campaign, when they reached the quarter-finals.

Jagiellonia Bialystok enter Thursday’s game on the back of a three-match winning run – a streak which has brought some much-needed relief and stability for head coach Adrian Siemieniec.

September and October turned out to be challenging months, with Jaga enduring a run of seven defeats from nine games at one point.

Off the pitch, the club was also embroiled in major controversy after Siemieniec received a six-match ban and a €20,000 (£16,700) fine for contacting a match official ahead of the penultimate game of last season.

However, two Ekstraklasa wins and a 6-0 thrashing of Lechia Gdansk in the Polish Cup have lately boosted spirits in Bialystok, as the club look to make serious progress in Europe.

As things stand, Jaga remain just outside the top 24 in the Europa League after collecting three points from their opening three games.

Their 3-1 victory over Ararat-Armenia was sandwiched between a 2-1 defeat to Olympiacos and a painful 3-0 thrashing at the hands of Anderlecht a fortnight ago.

Jagiellonia will now hope to strengthen their hopes of reaching the knockout stage when they face Bulgarian opposition for the first time in their history.

#1738. Wesley Fofana has a shot at redemption after shocking first half in Man United win, Estevao cements his status as Chelsea's fan favourite - and why Romeo Lavia was their star man, writes KIERAN GILL

Published: 02:01 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 04:27 EDT, 1 November 2026

There is something called the Science of Scare Project.

It is a study ranking the most frightening films of all time by measuring an audience’s reaction to watching them. Via their average heart rate, highest spike, time between heartbeats, and so on.

Halloween enthusiasts consulting this year’s eerie list found the spookiest ever was a 2012 supernatural horror called Sinister. That received a 'Scare Score' of 96/100. It beat The Conjuring (88/100), Paranormal Activity (73/100), Texas Chainsaw Massacre (65/100), and so on.

If only the good folks behind this scientific study had hooked up the Chelsea fans at Stamford Bridge. It would have been intriguing to know the fluctuating activity of their hearts as they watched Wesley Fofana flirt with gifting Manchester United the opening goal.

We would have seen the spikes occur whenever he was involved. Chelsea’s major mistakes came from the 25-year-old Frenchman, who will be needed more while Maxence Lacroix is recovering from his hamstring injury.

Xabi Alonso has told us Lacroix is facing ‘a few weeks’ on the sidelines, but sources around the player have suggested he may not return until 2027. That information has also been stood up by the odd contact at the club.

Chelsea’s major mistakes came from the 25-year-old Frenchman, who will be needed more

Chelsea supporters were thrilled they got to watch Estevao (left) and now he has given Alonso a selection headache

Which is worrying for Alonso and Co. While Chelsea wound up winning 2-0 against an abysmal United team now hovering over the relegation zone, Fofana’s first half was a shocker.

First, he was burgled of the ball by the halfway line. Amad countered, and while he should have made more of the chance, he won a corner. United scored from this attacking phase, but Chelsea survived when VAR decided the scorer, Matheus Cunha, was offside.

Then, Fofana misjudged a long pass to leave Amad with only Mike Penders to beat. Chelsea got away with that one, too.

This followed what happened at Anfield on Wednesday when Chelsea exited the Carabao Cup. Fofana swapped football for volleyball at a Liverpool corner to hand them their penalty equaliser. At the shootout, he was the unfortunate soul who skied the decisive spot-kick to confirm defeat.

If Alonso had any other senior central defenders available on his bench, he might have made the change at half-time versus United. He did not, and so Fofana survived a hooking.

To Fofana’s credit, he calmed after the break. He was the one clattered to win Chelsea their penalty and earn Lisandro Martinez his second yellow. There was even a point towards the end, when Chelsea were leading 2-0 against United’s 10 men, that he was trying to pass from the back.

Bruno Fernandes stood in his way and so he simply nutmegged his opponent to find Valentin Barco. As Fofana jogged by Fernandes immediately afterwards, he rubbed it in a little, laughing at United’s captain with a little finger-wagging gesture.

That told us the confidence is there, though Chelsea fans will continue to fear he is a player too prone to a clanger, rather than a centre back who cost £75million from Leicester City in 2022.

Even before his errors here, there were pieces penned by other websites suggesting he should be seen as the worst signing of the BlueCo era. Thanks to his driving infringements, we know how much he earns, too. More than £200,000 per week, his lawyer had to tell Lavender Hill Magistrates' Court in January as his client reached a remarkable 50 points on his licence.

It is fair to say he has not lived up to the hype which accompanied his arrival with injuries having hampered his career. But here is a small chance at redemption. Lacroix may miss the remainder of 2026, and Fofana will be needed. Chelsea would love him to reduce his 'Scare Score' which, in the first half of this win over United, was rivalling Sinister’s record.

Those of us inside Stamford Bridge did not notice it. We thought Bryan Mbeumo had sent his shot straight into the crossbar. But then we saw Penders celebrating, and the slow-mo replays.

Penders got his fingertips to it. He stopped any chance it had of creeping underneath the crossbar to reduce the scoreline to 2-1. The 21-year-old Belgian earned this clean sheet.

It was good to see. He had a nightmare against Tottenham, there is no hiding from that. He punched a cross into his own goal to give Spurs their opener in that 2-0 defeat. But at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, he responded well. Then here against United, he would not be beaten.

There has been talk of Chelsea rushing back Martinez from his jaw injury, maybe by having him wear a protective mask. But Penders performing like this may mean that is not necessary.

The loudest cheer when the line-ups were announced was reserved for Estevao, followed by Stamford Bridge chanting ‘Stevo, Stevo’. They love him, and they are right to love him.

He had to wait a long time for his first Premier League start of the season. Arguably too long.

But he seized his opportunity. Estevao scored two goals – alas, both were disallowed for offside – but he was forever involved. Chelsea supporters were thrilled they got to watch him, and now, he has given Alonso a selection headache because it was a showing which said he should start more.

Daily Mail Sport reported in our Chelsea Confidential column this week how there had been no fallout between Alonso and Estevao, despite speculation suggesting otherwise. His exclusion from the line-up was down to tactical and technical decisions.

When Estevao thought he had scored for the second time, he ran over to Alonso to give him a hug. When substituted, there was another cuddle. All is fine in that relationship, even if the 19-year-old Brazilian is itching to play more.

Lavia was actually the best performer in this victory. It was his winning of the ball that led to Rogers scoring

Jordan Henderson fell ill and so was unable to start his sixth successive match for Chelsea.

But that afforded an opportunity to Romeo Lavia. He had completed his first full 90 in a competitive game for Chelsea at Liverpool in the Carabao Cup. Then, a day before this Premier League visit of United, he was told he would need to start again.

Despite TNT Sports being blinded by Morgan Rogers’ fine opener – they gave him the player-of-the-match award – Lavia was actually the best performer in this victory. It was his winning of the ball that led to Rogers scoring. He then completed yet another full 90. You wait for one bus, then two come along at once.

#1736. FC Twente vs Pafos FC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 03 Nov 2026 22:18, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 14:03

FC Twente and Pafos FC meet in matchday three of the UEFA Conference League league phase at De Grolsch Veste in Enschede on Thursday, and the home team are looking to make it three wins from three.

The Tukkers have won both of their matches and sit fifth with six points, while the Paphites are 27th with one point after a 3-1 defeat at Atalanta and a 1-1 home draw with Riga FC.

John van den Brom's side have started their league-phase campaign with a 1-0 home win over Thun and a 4-1 victory at Lincoln Red Imps, their first two successive wins in a major European campaign since 2001-02.

Ramiz Zerrouki scored the only goal against Thun five minutes after the Swiss champions were reduced to 10 men by a debatable red card, and Thomas van den Belt then scored twice in Gibraltar, where Wout Weghorst and Daouda Weidmann also found the net.

The Tukkers followed that by beating AZ 2-0 in Alkmaar on October 25, with Sondre Orjasaeter scoring in the 84th minute and substitute Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink adding his first Eredivisie goal in stoppage time.

Sunday’s 9-0 win at Excelsior was the biggest in the club’s Eredivisie history, with Weghorst scoring four times for the first time in his career and Orjasaeter becoming the first player to register five assists in an Eredivisie match since the statistic has been recorded.

The scoreline needs context, because Excelsior played 85 minutes with 10 men after Nesto Groen was sent off in the sixth minute for a high challenge on Robin Propper.

The wins at Lincoln, AZ and Excelsior came by a combined 15-1 and followed a 2-1 home defeat by Utrecht on October 18, which remains the Tukkers’ most recent loss in any competition.

Weghorst joined on a free transfer from Ajax in June, reuniting with technical director Erik ten Hag, and after a stuttering start that drew jeers from home supporters he has become the focal point, although a hamstring problem picked up at AZ meant he was taken off after 62 minutes at Excelsior.

Pafos are in the main draw of a European competition for a third consecutive season, having reached the Conference League last 16 in 2024-25 and the Champions League league phase in 2025-26.

This season they beat Hajduk Split 4-2 on aggregate in Europa League qualifying and then lost a third-round tie to Salzburg 4-3 on aggregate, after a 1-0 defeat in Austria and a 3-3 home draw in which they led 2-0 at half time and conceded three after the break.

They then went through against Dinamo City of Albania 5-3 on aggregate in the Conference League playoff round, drawing 1-1 away and winning 4-2 at home on August 27.

In the league phase, Atalanta led 3-0 at half time through Eljif Elmas, Giacomo Raspadori and Gianluca Scamacca on the way to a 3-1 win on October 15, and Biel’s 76th-minute left-footed finish earned a 1-1 draw with Riga FC on October 22 after Caio Ferreira had given the visitors the lead in the 67th minute.

Pafos have conceded in each of their last six European matches, 11 goals in total, a run that includes three against Atalanta and three in the second half of the return leg against Salzburg.

Pafos drew 2-2 at Apollon Limassol on October 31, with Lele giving them the lead after half an hour and substitute Anderson Silva equalising late, which left them winless in four matches in all competitions after the Atalanta defeat and goalless and 1-1 draws with APOEL Nicosia and Riga.

Director Haris Theocharous told Cypriot outlet Goal that the club is not scoring from any area of the pitch and wants a restart, although he said head coach Ricardo Sa Pinto’s position is not under pressure.

Sa Pinto, who succeeded Albert Celades, leads a squad that finished fourth in the Cypriot First Division last season on 62 points and won the Cypriot Cup, with Anderson Silva scoring 14 goals in all competitions and Joao Correia 10 in the league.

Twente are without goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall, defenders Max Bruns and Stav Lemkin, and winger Filip Thorvaldsen, who has a knee injury, and none of the four is expected back before the international break.

Ruud Nijstad and Propper have formed the centre-back pairing in the absence of Bruns and Lemkin, with 18-year-old Jip Meilink making his debut at Lincoln, while Joel Drommel has kept goal in the league phase.

Weidmann served his Eredivisie suspension at Excelsior after a second yellow card at AZ and is expected to be available again, although Van den Belt, who has three goals across the Lincoln and Excelsior games, has done enough to keep his place.

Weghorst and Orjasaeter were both taken off after roughly an hour at Excelsior as part of a plan agreed at half time, and with Ajax visiting Enschede on Sunday, Van den Brom may manage their minutes again.

Pafos have a long injury list, with goalkeeper Jay Gorter and forward Jaja out long term, David Goldar, Nicolas Ngamaleu and Pepe among those who have missed recent weeks, and Jonatas Noro ruled out in late October.

David Luiz and Biel were reported to have fitness complaints last weekend, but Luiz returned to the starting lineup at Apollon Limassol and Radoslaw Majecki has kept goal in Gorter’s absence, so Sa Pinto is expected to start from the lineup that faced Riga.

Silva came off the bench at Apollon Limassol after starting against Riga, which suggests Sa Pinto may rotate his attack again, with Lele pushing for a place after his goal.

Drommel; Van Rooij, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Taha, Van den Belt; Rots, Orjasaeter, Weghorst

Majecki; Bruno, Mmaee, Luiz, Ioannou; Guga, Dragomir, Brito; Correia, Biel, Anderson Silva

Pafos have conceded in each of their last six European matches, including falling 3-0 behind at half time against Atalanta and surrendering a 2-0 lead against Salzburg, which represents a worrying defensive record ahead of facing a Twente side that have scored 15 goals across their last three away matches.

However, Twente benefited from playing against 10 men for long spells in their matches against Thun and Excelsior, while they are also without four injured players, and with Pafos scoring in five of their last six European fixtures, the hosts are backed to find the net, although a heavy defeat remains difficult to rule out.

#1735. Harry Kane embraces his family during special Ballon d'Or presentation at Bayern Munich - before England skipper MISSES a penalty in chaotic draw!

Published: 06:28 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 06:29 EDT, 1 November 2026

Harry Kane received a hero's welcome as he returned to action for Bayern Munich for the first time since winning the Ballon d'Or.

Kane was crowned as the best player in the world on Monday night, becoming the first English player to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001 on what was an emotional evening for the former Tottenham star.

His success came off the back of a stunning year with Bayern and England, with the forward netting a staggering 73 goals during the 2025-26 season.

Kane's goals spearheaded the German side's domestic Treble, while he also captained his country to third place at the World Cup.

And, ahead of Bayern's clash against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday night, Kane received a special presentation at the Allianz Arena.

With both sets of players and match officials lined up on the pitch, Kane was welcomed out of the tunnel while holding his new prized possession in his hands.

Harry Kane presented his Ballon d'Or trophy to Bayern Munich fans and players on Saturday

Kane received a hero's welcome from Bayern fans and his team-mates as he walked out

Kane was also greeted by his family, including his four children, ahead of the match

Bayern's players and fans gave Kane a standing ovation as Land of Hope and Glory played over the stadium's sound system.

The England skipper was serenaded by the home faithful, although some Dortmund fans could be heard to be booing him.

Waiting on the pitch were his family, including his wife Kate, four children, his parents and his brother Charlie, and he greeted them all as he came out.

Kane then took a microphone and addressed the home fans by saying: 'I’m extremely proud to be a Bayern player.

'The support you’ve shown me since I arrived is incredible. I’m extremely proud to present this to you. I hope to win many more titles with you.'

Unfortunately for Kane, his on-pitch return didn't perhaps go as planned as he missed a penalty as Bayern drew 2-2 with Dortmund.

Kane had the chance to mark his honour further after Konrad Laimer had put Bayern ahead, but he smacked his spot kick against the bar.

Serhou Guirassy then equalised for Dortmund, and although Kane assisted Dayot Upemecano's response, which put his side 2-1 up, former Wolves flop Fabio Silva equalised for the visitors in the 89th minute.

Kane addressed the crowd on the pitch where he highlighted his pride at playing for Bayern

Meanwhile, after winning the award on Monday, Kane had made sure to pay tribute to Bayern.

He said: 'Without you guys [Bayern Munich team-mates] and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete, so thank you very much.

'To Vinny [Vincent Kompany]. I know he is at home or still in the hospital. Wishing you well. I hope this gave you a bit of energy. To all the staff, the we way train and the way you push us, it is a credit to yourself.

'Since I have been with you I have improved as a player, improved as a person and a leader.

'It is an honour to play for Bayern Munich, to represent you is a real privilege and I am glad to be bringing this trophy back to Bayern Munich.'

#1733. ‘He looks like Rudiger’ - former coach on Real Madrid youngster Lamini Fati

By Alexis Pereira | 03 Nov 2026 22:25, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 23:00

Real Madrid already have a ‘mini-Rudiger’ in Castilla defender Lamini Fati, according to his former coach. Manolo Rueda, who managed the 20-year-old in Leganes’ Under-19s, has told AS that he sees a future Real Madrid first-team centre-back.

Fati is a jewel of La Fabrica. The Spain youth centre-back joined the academy in the summer of 2025 from Leganes and has already made his first appearances for the senior team under boss Jose Mourinho in pre-season.

After starting the season on the bench, Fati has played the last three Castilla games and made his first start against Algeciras (2-0) on 25 October. He was already mentioned in March as a possible solution to a defensive injury crisis, but he appears to need to establish himself in the reserves before hoping to join Mourinho’s squad.

Rueda explained Fati’s characteristics. ‘The quality that stands out most is the security and power he brings to the game. And a characteristic that I think is very underrated is his heading. I think he is very, very, very good in the air in attack. He scores goals and, defensively, he is very forceful.’

To break into Real Madrid’s defensive rotation, Fati has some points to improve. ‘I think Lamini has to bring continuity and speed in actions with the ball,’ Rueda said. ‘Without the ball, he has everything he needs. He has to refine some technical and tactical aspects, but he will get there with age, games and accumulated minutes.’

The 46-year-old sees a bright future. ‘Real Madrid currently have two excellent centre-backs in their squad, Konate and Rudiger. He looks a lot like them and could pair up with either. That is why I think he has a genuine chance of becoming a starting defender at Real Madrid.’

Fati may not get the chance to partner Rudiger, whose contract runs out at the end of the season, aged 33, but he could potentially replace him. ‘He is a player who looks like Rudiger,’ Rueda said. ‘He is aggressive in duels and simplifies actions with the ball. Both have very clear ideas and can execute their tasks at a very high level. Lamini needs to reach that level. If he can reproduce those efforts and behaviours at excellence, we could see “a mini-Rudiger”.’

#1732. Barcelona eye Arsenal’s Hincapie as January centre-back option

By Alexis Pereira | 03 Nov 2026 22:37

Barcelona, also recently linked with Paris SG Willian Pacho, have contacted the representatives of Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie as they plan to sign a centre-back in the January transfer window, with boss Hansi Flick said to approve of the Ecuadorian’s profile.

Barcelona are already looking ahead to the winter market, which opens in a little under two months. A first shortlist of four names has been revealed, featuring Alessandro Bastoni, Josko Gvardiol, Natan and Lisandro Martinez, but Actualite Barca, relayed by Sport, says Hincapie is also a target.

Hincapie signed permanently for Arsenal last summer for £34m, after a season on loan with the Gunners. Despite that and the absence of William Saliba since the start of the campaign, the 24-year-old has played little, making seven appearances with only two starts.

His profile still matches what Barcelona want. Flick likes his versatility between centre-back and left-back, a quality that could prove useful if Alejandro Balde leaves in January, as expected.

Sporting director Deco has already established first contact with the player’s entourage, aiming to gauge his willingness to move and explore a winter exit.

The deal will not be simple, however. Boss Mikel Arteta does not view Hincapie, who came from Bayer Leverkusen in 2024, as a regular starter, but he values the player and will be reluctant to let him leave mid-season. Arsenal will also not want to take a loss on the transfer, so they would ask for at least £34m, a significant sum for Barcelona’s finances.

#1731. Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal

For much of this sticky night in Naples, Arsenal appeared to be starting the new Champions League campaign the same way they finished the last one: by erroneously smashing the ball into the stands behind the goal.

Memories of Gabriel Magalhães’s ballooned penalty in the final against Paris St-Germain remain fresh in the mind, and here his team-mates were lining up to produce their own versions. Bukayo Saka and Piero Hincapié, especially, delivered astonishing misses which were closer to entering orbit than the opposition net.

Thankfully for Arsenal, though, there was one player who was in no mood to relive the frustration of that shoot-out loss 14 weeks ago. Martin Odegaard has started this season in truly fabulous form and here he scored a truly fabulous late goal, fizzed into the corner from range, to cap another inventive individual performance and earn three points for his team.

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

There was, almost inevitably, another clean sheet for Arteta’s side. They had the best defence in the Champions League last season, conceding only seven goals in 15 matches, and they were largely untroubled here. Ezri Konsa was once again excellent, in only his second start for the club. He successfully wrapped up Rasmus Hojlund, the former Manchester United centre-forward, and was as calm in possession as the absent William Saliba would have been. A potential injury to right-back Ben White was a concern, though.

The Champions League is the one that Arsenal have never won and, you suspect, the one that Arteta really wants. Success in this competition would elevate Arsenal to a higher level as a club and fully establish Arteta as one of the great coaching minds of his generation.

To lose last season’s final in such painful circumstances clearly hurt the Arsenal manager, who was visibly distraught after that shoot-out defeat despite the obvious delight of winning the Premier League title. If you could give him the choice between retaining the league this season or leading Arsenal to their first European Cup, he would surely pick the latter.

Arsenal have now won THIRTEEN UCL League Phase games in a row 🔴🔥 pic.twitter.com/UmcfMYO13r

A trip to Naples in the first round of the league phase made for a lovely opening tie: atmospheric, intense and competitive. Napoli have had a difficult start to their campaign, losing two of three Serie A games so far, but they possess real quality and have a top manager in Massimiliano Allegri.

Even at the age of 35, the great Kevin De Bruyne still has power in his boots and schemes in his mind. When he tested Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya from range in the first half, it would have triggered horrible flashbacks in the minds of the travelling supporters. In his previous 17 starts against Arsenal for Manchester City, De Bruyne had scored eight goals and registered four assists. Thankfully for Arsenal, it was the only moment in which De Bruyne really threatened.

Throughout this game, Arsenal moved the ball around with precision and purpose. They created an extraordinary amount of chances, with Saka and Hincapié missing the best of them. Saka’s effort in the first half, when one-v-one with the goalkeeper, was strangely erratic. Hincapié’s opportunity, meanwhile, was laughable. Two yards out from goal, he somehow put the ball onto the running track that surrounds the pitch at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

Despite all the wasted chances, Arsenal kept going. Odegaard, in particular, kept probing. His goal was gorgeous: a swift exchange of passes between him, White and Christos Tzolis resulted in the Arsenal captain firing his effort from the edge of the area. Delicate build-up, ferocious finish.

In keeping with the theme of the night, Arsenal should have scored more. Noni Madueke, for example, missed a one-v-one when it seemed like he had all the time in the world. But Odegaard’s intervention eventually proved to be enough, as he once again stood forward as Arsenal’s match-winner.

That’s all from us, but we’ll be back tomorrow night to bring you Man Utd’s return to the Champions League against Sabah!

"I think the chemistry, especially in the front players, has been exceptional." ✨Mikel Arteta tells @AnitaNnekaJones how impressed he's been by the connection between Martin Ødegaard and Christos Tzolis 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J6VOAMk4Lm

Arsenal extend their #UCL unbeaten streak 👏 pic.twitter.com/wFBga6lNrN

"We missed so many big chances"Mikel Arteta shares his thoughts after Arsenal's victory over Napoli 💭🎙️ @DannyJamieson | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zT2bHcPoiH

Before all of that, Arsenal will now have to turn their attention to the Stadium of Light as they travel to Sunderland on Saturday.

They then face Ipswich Town in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, before travelling to Brighton on the weekend.

Tue, November 24: Borussia Dortmund (H) 8pm

“Everything runs through Martin Odegaard,” said Cole on TNT Sports. “He can stand still and find space. He is at the peak of his powers and it is beautiful to watch.

“You can’t help but love watching him play his football.”

Plenty of praise for Martin Odegaard on TNT, with former Arsenal man Martin Keown heralding the captain’s behaviour.

“He’s setting an example to his players. He’s fitter, he’s hungry, and he did his talking on the pitch. He came good for his team.”

Couple that with his impressive chemistry with new arrival Christos Tzolis, and there is a lot of goal-scoring potential there this season. Three of the winger’s four assists have been for his captain, and we’re barely a month into the season.

The action has concluded around Europe tonight so here are your final scores from this week’s second night of European football:

Napoli did not register a shot on target in that second half, and it is clear how much Arsenal just dominated to keep the pressure on.

It could easily have been three or four goals for Arsenal had they had better finishing, but either way, they did not let their heads go down.

They kept pushing to see out the result and got the job done. Arteta will be very happy with that away result.

This has not been Arsenal’s most clinical performance but they got the job done.

Here is the goal that won it for them, courtesy of their captain:

Great play 😮‍💨Martin Ødegaard rounds off a wonderful passing move for Arsenal 🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FrH6gW8Ak4

Napoli are fighting, but Arsenal hold fast.

Milinković-Savić waves his players downfield for the final minute but Olivera can’t control the ball well.

Four minutes will be added on here as Napoli are being urged on by their fans.

Arsenal need to hold onto the ball and manage the game intelligently here. Zubimendi goes in for a challenge though and hauls down his man, and Napoli get the ball back. Odegaard goes into the book for his protests.

Napoli again, still trying to get their goal and De Bruyne gives them a chance with a through ball to David Neres, but the striker can’t get on the ball.

Arsenal are almost caught as the ball falls to De Bruyne on the left of the box, with a clear look at Raya in goal, but the Belgian crosses the ball thinking he’s got a team-mate there to put it away but there is no one and it is a huge let-off for Arsenal.

Napoli with every man forward lose the ball and suddenly Zubimendi finds himself on the break. With Madueke on his right, he feeds the winger who gets into space in the box to be one-on-one with Milinković-Savić. But the Arsenal man hesitates and the keeper spreads himself, blocking Madueke’s eventual shot. He can’t turn around to get on the rebound and cuts is back for Tzolis, whose own shot is then blocked.

With just a few minutes to go, Arsenal make their final change.

Ben White appeared to be in a little bit of discomfort a few minutes ago. He’s now been replaced by Martin Zubimendi for the final 10 minutes of this game. Declan Rice appears to have moved to right-back.

Martin Odegaard has played some outstanding football tonight (again) and that is an absolutely outstanding goal. The delicacy of the build-up and then the ferocity of the finish. Four goals in five games for Odegaard this season.

There will be alarm bells ringing for Allegri and Napoli, as they are heading for their third defeat on the trot. They have not created much of anything in this second half and you have to imagine that Arsenal will now make life very difficult for them.

To be exact, they have had a grand total of one shot in the second half.

Napoli will have to push now, and make more changes, bringing on Lorenzo Lucca and David Neres for Rasmus Hojlund and Stanislav Lobotka.

The breakthrough comes and of course it is Odegaard! Finally they get their moment, hacing recycled the ball on the edge of the area.

Rice just passes it out to him off a nice ball from Tzolis and the captain rifles a low shot into the far bottom corner.

Rice loses the ball in midfield and fouls Olivera as he tries to recover it.

Before they take the free kick though, Arsenal make more changes. Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke come on for Gyokeres and Saka.

Guimaraes to Saka before the winger sends the ball back to Odegaard on the edge of the box. He lifts a ball into the centre of the box where there are a lot of bodies, but Tzolis snatches at it and sends the ball into the rafters.

Sums up the game so far really for Arsenal.

There is definitely a goal in here somewhere. Napoli are still waiting and searching for their goal, and Arsenal will keep throwing shots at the wall until something sticks.

There are the subs, Mikel Merino and Eberechi Eze are the ones to make way.

Christos Tzolis and Bruno Guimaraes getting ready to come on.

At the same time, Favasuli makes a neat little run on the right trying to get to the touchline and pull the ball back, but Raya is able to pick it up easily.

That was almost it for Napoli, Hojlund with a great run in behind. He gets into the box one-on-one against his defender as Raya retreats. The challenge is perfectly timed though as he tries to get his shot off and the ball goes spinning off to the side.

Neither side are looking clinical in front of goal though as Arsenal take the ball down the other end, and Declan Rice can only send another shot over the bar.

Saka tries to take another chance on the edge of the box, but he loses the ball.

Napoli try to seize their moment on the break, with Favasuli releasing down the left side. He looks for Hojlund in the middle of the field, but his cross is just not good enough and Raya comes out to collect the high ball.

Politano and Alisson Santos make way for Antonio Vergara and Constantino Favasuli.

Though the hosts came out on the front foot, it has been all Arsenal since then, so Allegri will be hoping these changes can shift the momentum.

Alisson Santos gets past White on the sideline, and makes the run down the left. He tries to find De Bruyne making the run in the middle but it is intercepted and Arsenal take the ball back up the field.

Napoli are getting ready to make some changes.

Arsenal probing again, with Rice, Saka, Odegaard and White exchanging passes on the right edge of the box. Saka tries a low ball in but it’s blocked before it gets to Gyokeres.

Napoli are sitting so deep, you have to assume they are just waiting for an opportunity to counter. Even so, Arsenal are doing well to keep the ball moving around and try and find space. The hosts are really trying not to concede first.

Another wasted chance for Arsenal! Great play from Odegaard lifting a little ball into the centre of the box, which is flicked on towards goal. It falls to Hincapié in the six-yard box but as he tries to poke it into the goal, the Ecuadorian sends it flying over the bar.

Napoli have every man behind the ball right now as Arsenal get some possession.

Arsenal’s turn now, as White gets himself into a good position on the right side of the box, exchanging passes with Odegaard and Saka.

Saka tries to send a ball into the box, but it’s blocked and sent out the sideline as Napoli remain disciplined and shut down the space.

That momentum falls apart for Napoli as Oliveira fouls Gyokeres as the strikers comes in to defend.

Napoli are starting with some pressure here..

Napoli have changed their keepers at half-time. Meret received some treatment in the first half and has been taken off, replaced by Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. It’s his first appearance of the season.

Arsenal with the better of the first half, but unable to find the breakthrough.

Liverpool have equalised at Anfield after Marcos Llorente put Atlético Madrid ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai is the man to put the ball in the back of the net – to the great relief of Andoni Iraola I’m sure.

Reigning champions PSG are 3-0 up against Slovan, with a quick double coming from Mr Ballon D’or himself, Ousmane Dembélé. Ferran Torres scored the third.

Sporting vs Galatasaray also level at 1-1 so it’s really all to play for in the next 45 minutes. Stay tuned!

That’s the final action of the half, and nothing separates the two sides at the break. Both with three shots on target, though Arsenal have taken 13 shots to Napoli’s four.

Both teams could have stolen a goal to take the lead, but they will have to wait for the second period for the opportunity.

Arsenal get a corner which is delivered really well to the far post, but as it’s headed in, there is no space for White to turn and shoot from the six-yard box. He tries to lay it off for Hincapié but Meret gets low to grab it.

Arsenal have created more than enough chances to be three or four goals clear here. That miss by Saka was the best one yet, and the England winger will be in disbelief at the spooned nature of his finish. It looked a certain goal. Shocker.

Arsenal get another great chance as Odegaard sends a perfect ball to Saka as he makes the run into the box on the right side. The winger stays onside but Lobotka does enough to put him off and Saka sends it over the bar.

Napoli are first into the book as Gilmour fouls Eze 35 yards out.

Arsenal take the free kick but end up passing the ball around the edge of the box. Eventually Odegaard lifts a high ball into the box, but Meret punches it away confidently.

Konsa does really well to hold up Alisson Santos as he makes a very speedy run down the left, keeping him from sending a ball into the box.

The game is opening up now, as Saka makes a run of his own down the right, with Gyokeres in the box but Napoli keep tight and Rrahmani does well to stop the ball reaching the striker.

A good save from Raya as Hojlund again feeds the wings from the centre of the field. Politano makes a great run in from the right side with the ball and takes a curling shot with his left foot on the edge of the box.

Arsenal’s keeper collects and then minutes later his side have a shot of their own, but Saka can only send it over the bar.

Saka again gets enough time on the right edge of the box to send a low ball to Rice in the right corner. His shot goes over the bar and we’re having an impromptu drinks break as Meret gets some treatment.

Treat yourself to a hydration break of your own.

Napoli coming close as Hojlund fed in the centre, one-on-one with Konsa, trying to turn at the top of the box. He dinks the ball into the path of the running De Bruyne, whose shot is blocked by Konsa, who scrambles back quickly.

Hincapié sends a cross in from the left which almost catches Meret out at the near post as the keeper scrambles across to push it away.

Now it’s Napoli’s turn as Lobotka sends a long ball down the left to Alisson Santos, who sends a great cross in to the box. Konsa just does enough to put him off and it meets Rice in the centre of the box, for the midfielder to clear.

Saka comes in again on his left foot, with a series of short passes between Odegaard and Rice, but his shot is blocked as two defenders shut him down.

Another attempt for Arsenal as Odegaard gets forward and passes to Eze on the left wing. He drives in and takes a shot with his right foot from just inside the box, but he drags it wide of the target.

Good start to this game. Plenty going on. Arsenal look dangerous and capable of pinning Napoli deep into their own half, but the Italians have threatened on the break. De Bruyne’s shot from range would have triggered some nasty flashbacks for the Arsenal fans but, thankfully for them, it was straight at Raya.

Great chance from Arsenal as Eze pulls away at the back post and connects with the ball to send a header into the box. Merino connects with a diving header of his own but it’s straight at Meret and tipped over the bar.

Arsenal again biding their time until Rice plays a neat ball to White on the right edge of the boxm which he lifts into the box. No one around to do anything with it and Meret collects.

Arsenal being patient on the edge of the box moving the ball around, but eventually it breaks down with Eze losing the ball and then fouling De Bruyne as he tries to break away.

The Napoli players feel that should have been a card.

Di Lorenzo again looks to find space down the centre of the field but sends the ball out to Politano again on the right wing, who lofts a very high ball towards the back post but Raya collects with confidence.

Di Lorenzo makes a great run onto a long ball on the left side, racing down the sideline. He sends a ball across to find De Bruyne in the centre of the field, and the midfielder takes a great shot, which Raya can’t hold on to. White reacts to clear but Napoli are having a good spell.

Politano is the next to force a save from the Arsenal keeper with a shot from the right corner of the box, keeping their visitors very much on their toes.

Arsenal dominating possession in the early stages, just testing the Napoli defence. The stadium is quite quiet and we can hear the travelling fans declaring their love for their team.

Free kick for the visitors as Eze is fouled 40 yards out. Odegaard takes and sends a high ball into the centre of the box, which Gabriel can’t quite control.

Arsenal come again as Gyokeres sends a cross into the box from the left and Saka tries an overhead kick but it is straight into the centre of the goal and Meret has little trouble.

Rice again but the keeper comes to collect and sets the counter free.

Hojlund makes a great run and feeds Alisson Santos on the left side. He tries to cut in but is well marked by White and he can only send his shot over the bar from inside the box.

Arsenal get their first corner as Eze finds himself in a central position at the top of the box, and plays neat one-two with Gyokeres, but his shot takes a big deflection.

Rice goes to the corner flag, and sends in a good ball, headed out by Napoli for another corner.

Arsenal probing on the right wing, with White, Odegaard and Saka overlapping nicely. The captain feeds White and he passes in a neat little ball to Saka just inside the box. He tries a shot, but it’s blocked.

Napoli are getting back very quickly when Arsenal are pressing.

Marín sends a nice high ball across the field to find Politano on the right side. He feeds De Bruyne on the edge of the box and the Belgian tries a shot at Raya, curling it with his right foot, but with not much on it, Raya collects in the middle of goal.

Both teams getting little spells on the ball to get going.

Arsenal are keeping tight as Napoli try and play the ball out from the back and the long ball out to Hojlund is easily collected for Raya.

You can hear the Arsenal fans in loud voice, accompanied by plenty of jeers and whistles from the home fans.

The players are lining up around the centre circle, with a minute of silence for the victims of the tragedy in Nepal.

I wrote a little while ago that it was an unpleasantly warm evening in Naples. I now want to revise that comment. It’s nastily hot, and it’s getting worse. The air is thick (27 degrees and 74 per cent humidity, according to my weather app) and I can’t imagine it will be easy for the players.

“Every game starts at 0-0, but clearly Arsenal are favourites. We’ll need to show our strength and ability to be competitive. We’ll approach the game with determination and pride as we try to get a positive result.

These two sides haven’t met since the 2018-19 Europa League quarter-finals, when Alexandre Lacazette sent Arsenal through to the last four with a cracking goal.

Arsenal have only travelled to Naples once in the Champions League, back in 2013, which saw the home side win 2-0 and then Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta get sent off with two yellows. Arsenal still made it out of the group stages that year, helped by their own 2-0 win when the Italians came to N5.

“We know what this competition means to all of us, the experience of last year as well, so we need to start with the first game in a really, really tough place, but really excited to start the campaign.

“It will be a really tough place, I’ve been in that stadium before, I know the atmosphere they create, their record at home is really, really strong. They have a very experienced manager, a lot of players that played in the league as well, so we know the challenge ahead. We are prepared and we’re ready to go.”

Two matches kicked off at 5.45pm, and with just under half an hour to go:

The visitors are still without Cristhian Mosquera, who picked up an injury against Aston Villa, and Jurrien Timber – though the right-back has rejoined first-team training and travelled with the squad to Italy. William Saliba remains their only long-term absentee as he recovers from a back injury.

Naples have a few more players out of action. As well as McTominay, centre-back Alessandro Buongiorno is still sidelined following a knee procedure over summer and Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa is missing with a groin injury.

Strikers Giovane and David Neres are dealing with hernia and knee problems respectively, while youngster Luca Marianucci is on his way back after a knee injury in pre-season.

Napoli have not started the season particularly well, losing two of their three Serie A games so far. But they do have a player who has a long history of hurting Arsenal: the great Kevin De Bruyne. The former Manchester City midfielder has been directly involved in 12 goals in his last 17 starts against Arsenal across all competitions (8 goals, 4 assists), including five in his most recent three (3 goals, 2 assists). Now 35 though, he is not the force he once was.

Arsenal’s Champions League campaign last year ended in the most agonising of penalty shoot-out defeats but that should not detract from the brilliance of their run to the final. Mikel Arteta’s side were the only team who didn’t lose a single game in normal time in this competition last season, and also conceded only seven goals all season — the fewest of any team in the competition, despite the fact they played 15 matches.

Mikel Arteta has made four changes to the team that defeated Chelsea on Sunday. Piero Hincapie comes in for Riccardo Calafiori, Mikel Merino for Myles Lewis-Skelly, Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis and Viktor Gyokeres for Kai Havertz.
