Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

Barcelona are reportedly keeping a close eye on Tottenham Hotspur midfielder Lucas Bergvall as uncertainty grows over his role in Roberto De Zerbi’s side.

The Swedish international has faced increased competition for minutes following Tottenham’s summer recruitment, while Barcelona and Napoli are understood to be monitoring his situation.

According to TEAMtalk, Barcelona are among the clubs interested in Bergvall, with Napoli also linked with the 20-year-old midfielder.

Bergvall has started only twice in the Premier League this season, with the arrivals of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes increasing competition in midfield. Despite signing a new long-term contract with Spurs recently, his limited league starts could attract further attention from potential suitors.

Barcelona have previously been linked with the Swedish talent, who is highly regarded for his technical ability and potential to develop into a top-level midfielder.

However, Tottenham are in a strong position to retain him following his contract extension, and there is no confirmation that Barcelona have submitted an offer.

Tottenham are also waiting to discover the extent of James Maddison’s latest injury after the midfielder was forced off during the 2-0 victory over Chelsea.

Maddison had only recently returned to the starting line-up after a lengthy absence, making the setback a concern for De Zerbi.

Speaking after the match, the Tottenham manager said: “I hope he didn’t feel a big problem, but we have to make a medical check.”

#1602. Oxford City vs Leicester City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 04 Nov 2026 16:25, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 22:11

Fallen giants Leicester City will be aiming to avoid what would be one of the biggest shocks in recent FA Cup history when they head to National League North outfit Oxford City on Friday night in the first round of the tournament.

It is the first time that Leicester have competed in this round since 2008, and Oxford City have been given the chance to claim a huge scalp in the tournament.

Oxford City have managed to progress to the second round of the FA Cup on three previous occasions - 1969-70, 2017-18 and 2020-21, so the club have previous when it comes to advancing past this stage of the famous cup competition.

The Hoops will enter this match off the back of a disappointing result, though, going down 3-1 at home to South Shields in the National League North on Saturday.

Ross Jenkins' side are currently second in the National League North, picking up 27 points from their opening 14 matches of the campaign, two points behind South Shields following the clash between the top two.

Oxford City have had to win three matches to reach this stage of the FA Cup, overcoming Dorchester, Enfield Town and Torquay to be present in the first round.

Leicester, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of a 2-2 draw with Stevenage, with the result leaving them in 10th spot in the League One table.

The Foxes have won three of their last five league games, but there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a disappointing start to the season as a whole.

Leicester famously won this competition back in 2021, recording a 1-0 victory over Chelsea courtesy of a second-half effort from Youri Tielemans.

Russell Martin is still under pressure at Leicester but remains at the helm, with the 40-year-old bidding to help the Foxes secure a return to the Championship.

Leicester's last FA Cup fixture brought a 2-1 defeat to Southampton in the last-16 stage of the 2025-26 competition.

Oxford City will be looking to Tyrone Marsh for goals on Friday, with the 32-year-old netting nine times in all competitions at the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

There will also be a position in the team for Scott Pollock, who has been another key performer this season, coming up with six goals and two assists in 13 appearances.

Ludwig Francillette and Josh Ashby are also set to be notable starters.

As for Leicester, there are set to be a number of changes to the team that took to the field for the 2-2 draw with Stevenage in the league last time out.

However, Ben Nelson and Jakub Stolarczyk are both out of the match through injury.

Conor Chaplin should be introduced in the final third of the field, while 19-year-old Ilari Kangasniemi is expected to be a notable starter at the back.

Fellow teenager Louis Page is expected to be among those to be rested.

Maxted; Nelson, Francillette, Carroll, Humphries; Tetek, Ashby; Bateman, Pollock, Brown; Marsh

McCarthy; Aluko, Souttar, Kangasniemi, Thomas; Lundstram, Neale; Howell, Chaplin, Watson; Bristric

We are not predicting an FA Cup shock on Friday night; Leicester should have too much quality for their National League North opponents in the first round of the tournament.

Arsenal are reportedly among the clubs keeping a close eye on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, whose outstanding start to the season has attracted interest from several major European sides.

The 21-year-old Portuguese forward has emerged as one of Serie A’s most exciting attacking prospects, with his goalscoring form reportedly putting him on the radar of Arsenal, Napoli and former club Benfica.

According to ⁠Calciomercato.it, Napoli could look to make a move for Varela during the January transfer window as they assess their attacking options.

However, Arsenal are also among the clubs monitoring the striker, with the Premier League side representing a significant threat to Napoli’s plans. Benfica are another interested party after allowing Varela to leave for Monza last summer.

Varela has scored seven goals in eight Serie A appearances, placing him at the top of the league’s goalscoring standings at the time of the report. His performances have helped establish him as a player attracting attention beyond Italy.

The forward joined Monza from Benfica in the summer, and his immediate impact has made the transfer look increasingly valuable for the Italian club.

Although Benfica no longer have Varela under contract, they reportedly retained the right to match a future offer for the striker, alongside a 20 per cent share of any profit Monza makes from a subsequent sale.

That arrangement could complicate negotiations for Arsenal or Napoli, although it does not automatically mean Benfica will bring the player back to Portugal.

Monza also have little obvious incentive to sell midway through the season. Varela has become an important player for the club, and his continued scoring could strengthen their negotiating position ahead of future transfer windows.

Varela’s finishing record and strong start in Italy explain why clubs are beginning to take notice. Arsenal’s reported interest suggests he is one of the forwards being monitored, but there is no confirmation that the Gunners have made a formal offer.

Napoli could explore a January approach, while Benfica’s contractual rights give them a potential role in any future deal.

What this means for Arsenal: Varela is a name worth watching as the transfer window approaches, but any potential move will depend on Monza’s willingness to negotiate and the level of competition from Napoli and Benfica. For now, the interest remains reported rather than a confirmed transfer pursuit.

#1598. Gaziantep vs Kasimpasa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 04 Nov 2026 16:42, Last updated: 04 Nov 2026 16:42

Gaziantep will be desperate to halt their alarming slide when they welcome Kasimpasa to Gaziantep Stadyumu on Friday in the Turkish Super Lig.

The hosts have lost five consecutive league matches and are hovering just above the relegation zone with eight points from their opening 10 fixtures, while their visitors occupy fifth place with 17 points and arrive unbeaten in their last three league outings.

Gaziantep have endured a miserable spell in the league, with their latest setback coming in a 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

Orhan Ak's side struggled to make an impact against the Black Sea outfit, conceding once in each half as they suffered another damaging result following defeats against Erzurumspor, Istanbul Basaksehir, Corum and Kocaelispor.

Their 4-0 Turkish Cup victory over Etimesgutspor provided some relief, but that result has done little to disguise their domestic difficulties, particularly as they have scored just twice across their last five league matches while conceding 12 goals.

The lack of attacking output is becoming a significant concern for Ak, whose team have struggled to turn possession into meaningful opportunities and have repeatedly found themselves chasing matches after falling behind.

Gaziantep have also struggled to establish Gaziantep Stadyumu as a source of points, failing to win any game as hosts yet, drawing two and losing three times in five home matches.

However, the Falcons are unbeaten in their last five meetings with the Apaches, picking up three wins and two draws, while they have also avoided defeat in their last three encounters against them as hosts, winning twice and drawing once.

Kasimpasa, meanwhile, have enjoyed a considerably more encouraging opening to the campaign, losing just one of their 10 league games so far while recording four wins and five draws.

Emre Belozoglu's team were held to an entertaining 2-2 draw by Besiktas in their previous league outing, with Claudio Winck and Michael Rafferty finding the net as they twice threatened to take all three points.

That result extended their unbeaten league sequence to three matches, following victories over Eyupspor and Samsunspor, while they also recorded a 3-1 win over Corluspor in the Turkish Cup, extending their unbeaten run across all competitions to four matches.

Kasimpasa have also collected useful points on their travels this season, recording 10 points from five away games, with three wins, one draw and one defeat, which should give them optimism ahead of this trip.

Gaziantep have several availability concerns ahead of Friday's encounter, with Myenty Abena facing suspension following a yellow-card accumulation, while Ulrich Meleke, Ogun Ozcicek, Arda Kizildag and Sontje Hansen are among those carrying injuries.

Serdar Dursun is also expected to miss out, while Nazim Sangare and Fuat Bavuk remain unavailable.

Kasimpasa have fewer confirmed concerns, although Kamil Ahmet Corekci is expected to remain sidelined with an Achilles tendon injury.

Godfried Frimpong and Kevin Mouanga are also carrying fitness problems, leaving the visitors potentially short of defensive options, while no further suspensions have been reported.

Adrian Benedyczak has scored six goals in the league this season, and he will be the man to watch for the Apaches in this encounter.

#1597. Manchester United targeting £70 million Newcastle star as January transfer hopes fade

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Manchester United remain interested in signing Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall, but securing his services could prove difficult after the left-back committed his future to the Magpies.

The England international was among United’s defensive targets during the summer transfer window.

However, Newcastle refused to entertain his departure, and his new contract has strengthened their position ahead of any potential negotiations.

Despite those obstacles, United continue to view Hall as a long-term option at left-back.

According to ⁠Football Insider, Manchester United would likely need to pay at least £70 million to persuade Newcastle to part with the 22-year-old.

Transfer correspondent Pete O’Rourke reports that Hall remains high on United’s list of targets, with the club continuing to monitor his situation.

O’Rourke explained: “They do like Lewis Hall and see him as somebody who could come in there and become a mainstay for them at left back for the foreseeable future in that side.”

Hall has since signed a contract extension that keeps him at St James’ Park until 2031. That agreement puts Newcastle in a strong negotiating position, meaning United would likely need to make a substantial offer to have any chance of completing a deal.

Newcastle regard Hall as an important part of their plans and are under no immediate pressure to sell the defender.

His performances for club and country have enhanced his reputation, while his long-term contract gives the Magpies greater control over his future.

Although United have continued to track the situation, a January departure is reportedly not expected. A move next summer appears more plausible, although Newcastle’s stance could make negotiations difficult then as well.

Hall is also believed to be settled at Newcastle, so United would need both clubs to reach an agreement and the player to remain open to the switch.

United’s interest reflects their desire to strengthen at left-back and find a long-term option for the position. Hall’s age, Premier League experience and potential make him an attractive candidate.

However, a fee exceeding £70 million would represent a significant investment, particularly with Newcastle having little incentive to negotiate a sale.

United may therefore have to consider alternative targets if the Magpies refuse to lower their demands.

#1596. CM: Dalot could reunite with Amorim at Milan as Man Utd deal winds down

Diogo Dalot has once again been linked with a potential return to AC Milan, where he spent the 2020-21 season on loan.

Calciomercato.com report that Roma’s visit to face Manchester United at Old Trafford will not only be an opportunity for the Giallorossi to face and perhaps erase the ghosts of the past, but also to watch someone up close who could be a name for the not-too-distant future: Diogo Dalot.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese full-back’s contract is expiring at the end of next season and although he is happy in Manchester, many clubs are beginning to ask his entourage for details.

Roma were one step away from landing the defender in the summer of 2021 when the Portuguese coach José Mourinho was on the bench. The negotiations dragged on for a long time, but in the end it didn’t go through.

The reason ended up being quite simple: the Red Devils never agreed to a loan with option to buy formula while Roma – who were still severely limited by Financial Fair Play limitations – could not offer anything more.

Dalot knows Italy and Serie A well, and he recently spoke about his loan experience with Milan in an interview with The Player’s Tribune.

“It was one of the most important years of my career. I remember the way the club welcomed me and how welcome I felt in a year that was important to me, one in which I needed to regain my confidence in my football. Milan helped me get back to those levels,” he said.

“Every day, Paolo Maldini was on the sidelines to watch us train. Rain, shine, or cold, he was always there, in a suit and tie. He would say to me: ‘Mark like this’ or ‘Tackle it.’ Other times, he would scold me for trying too hard. ‘You’re an extraordinary player, don’t worry, you’ll see, everything will be fine’.”

As mentioned, Dalot’s deal expires in 2028 but there is the presence of a one-year clause that United can trigger. There are a number of teams monitoring his situation including Inter, Milan and Juventus, who have all enquired in recent weeks.

Nothing concrete has emerged yet, as Dalot happy in Manchester and isn’t thinking about the future. However, if things don’t change, a departure – perhaps even for a low-cost fee – could become a realistic possibility.

With the Rossoneri needing defenders, could they try pounce on a reunion for a versatile player that they and Ruben Amorim know well?
